title: Repeat Purchase Rate
description: A customer is a **repeat buyer** if they made a purchase on at least **two different dates**. Report `repeat_customers` (the count of repeat buyers) and `total_customers` (the count of distinct customers who ever bought). Name the columns `repeat_customers`, `total_customers` and `rate` — the repeat share, `ROUND(repeat/total, 2)`. One row only.
solutionSql:
WITH buyer_days AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_date) AS days
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN days >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS repeat_customers,
  COUNT(*) AS total_customers,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN days >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS rate
FROM buyer_days;
hint: Count distinct *dates* per customer — two orders on the same day are still one visit. Then count who crossed the ≥2-day threshold.
outputExplanation: 3 customers total; customer 1 bought on 2 different days so counts as repeat → 1/3 = 0.33.
